messages:
samir: heads-up — CUST-382 reports p99 spikes on chat endpoints after last night's kernel/compileflag rollout (flash-pref=on). p95 ~450ms ok but p99 jumped 2200ms -> ~3200ms for a subset of requests. @oncall please triage.
oncall-bot: Alert: high p99 observed on prod chat routes (route: /v1/chat) — threshold breached. Alert group: eng-runtime.
jen: on it. can you paste a couple request ids + region so i can pull traces?
samir: sure — ids: req_01A2B3C4 (us-west-2), req_01D9E8F7 (eu-west-1)
samir: example span snippet: "model: gpt-open-16k, seq_len:1024, tokens: 768, kernel: flashattn, duration_ms: 3210"
marco: we pushed sdpa heuristic + flash-pref compileflag at 02:30 UTC last night. i'm going to check canary logs — if it's the kernel selection path we can force a fallback to the older kernel for chat quickly. repro steps?
samir: quick repro curl (prod, sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-16k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long context... ~1k tokens"}],"max_tokens":512}'
```
sequence: send 4 concurrent requests with seq ~1024, observe tail latencies.
li: i tried repro locally with seq=1024, batch=4 — p99 jumps when the routing picks flashattn for longseq. toggling compileflag off (rebuild) fixes p99 locally. i think --use-flash-pref is causing a kernel misselection on models with large KV caches.
tasha: mitigation plan: 1) throttle kernel routing for chat route to prefer "fallback" kernel variant, 2) enable aggressive kv-prefix caching for chat, 3) monitor p95/p99. i'll start a small canary 5% then 25%.
`tasha` command (rolling change):
```
redwood rollout update --route chat --kernel-priority fallback --kv-prefix true --env prod --percent 5
```
deploy-bot: Deploy started by tasha: rollout-id r-2026-03-17-01 (canary 5%)
jen: support, pinged the customer, told them we're investigating and performing mitigations; ETA ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
support: ack — notifying CUST-382: "we're seeing a p99 regression for some long-context requests after a kernel heuristic change; mitigation in progress, we'll update in ~30m"
marco: collecting perf profiles and kernel selection logs now. if the kernel-priority rollback doesn't help, next step is to back out compileflag from the image and redeploy a build without flash-pref.
li: also adding a short test to kerneltuner to avoid selecting flashattn for seq>800 for this model family. PR incoming.
samir: thanks all — i'll paste post-rollout numbers when canary finishes. adding the two trace ids to the incident ticket.
jen: good. keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
